consolidation_summary.reason: 'Menstruation' (main-chapter physiology section) and 'Menstrual Cycle' (a same-topic appendix entry under the mislabeled terminal GY.S18 'References' section) cover the same normal-physiology content; consolidated rather than duplicated as two units.

'Imaging' and 'Endometrial Biopsy' are consolidated as the non-surgical investigation pair under 'Common Investigations and Procedures'; 'Hysterectomy' (T03) is split out separately since it is a therapeutic procedure with distinct indications/complications evidence, not an investigation.

'First Trimester Bleeding' and 'Spontaneous Abortions' are two facets of one presentation-to-diagnosis pathway sharing MCC objective 81; consolidated rather than split since MCC has no per-facet objective.
'Female Factors' and 'Male Factors' are two facets of the single couple-level infertility competency (MCC objective 46); consolidated rather than split.

'Physiologic Discharge', 'Non-Physiologic Discharge', and 'Vulvovaginitis' are three facets of the single vaginal-discharge differential targeted by MCC objective 113; consolidated, while the section's five clinically distinct T-children (STI, Bartholin Gland Abscess, PID, Toxic Shock Syndrome, Surgical Infections) were each kept as independent units.
'Premenstrual Syndrome' and 'Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder' are both named and explicitly differentiated within the single MCC objective 56-3; consolidated as one unit rather than two.

title_mismatch_notes.note: GY.S01's printed TOC title 'Acromyms' is a garbled/trivial rendering of 'Acronyms' (an acronym list, not a clinical topic); merged_duplicate_headings records the legible alternate 'Basic Anatomy Review', used as the study-unit title, mirroring the GM.S01 precedent of preferring a legible source-confirmed alternate over a garbled/non-substantive printed one.

GY.S04 ('Disorders of Menstruation') carries merged_duplicate_headings 'Endometriosis' and 'Adenomyosis' alongside its three T-children (Amenorrhea, Abnormal Uterine Bleeding, Dysmenorrhea). Unlike the GM.S05/GM.S01-style merges (alternate labels for the SAME content), these are clinically distinct diagnoses with no dedicated child node; each is broken out into its own study unit cited against the parent section node rather than silently dropped or folded into an existing T-child.

GY.S05's printed title 'Fibroids' (BODY_HEADING_CONFIRMATION) conflicts with all three of its own T-children (Hormonal Methods, IUD, Emergency Postcoital Contraception), which unambiguously match its merged_duplicate_headings entry 'Contraception'. The section is represented as Contraception; Fibroids/uterine leiomyoma is NOT fabricated as a separate study unit since no source node in this inventory carries fibroid content - see unrecoverable_coverage_gaps below.

GY.S12's printed title 'SexualAbuse' with merged_duplicate_headings 'Sexuality and Sexual Dysfunction' names two clinically distinct topics (forensic sexual abuse/assault vs. clinical sexual dysfunction), not one topic under two labels; split into two units, both cited against the shared parent node.

GY.S18's printed title 'References' is a structural mislabel: unlike the genuine terminal bibliography sections in every other completed chapter, its four T-children (Menstrual Cycle, Stages of Puberty, Premenstrual Syndrome, Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder) are real appendix-style clinical content. Each is represented under its own real topic rather than dismissed as bibliographic reference material.
